chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked about the sun: does it purify the ground? He said: If a place is filthy from urine or something else, and the sun reaches it, then the place dries, salat on that place is permissible. But if the sun reaches it and the filthy place does not dry and remains moist, then salat on it is not permissible until it dries. And if your foot is moist, or your forehead is moist, or some other part of you that touches that filthy place is moist, then do not perform salat on that. And if something other than the sun reaches it until it dries, then that is not permissible.

key_terms.الشَّمْسِ: the sun, whose drying effect is treated here as a means connected to purification of the ground
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), whose validity on that surface is being addressed
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the ground or earth that has been affected by impurity
key_terms.الْبَوْلِ: urine, mentioned as a source of ritual impurity
key_terms.تُطَهِّرُ: purifies; renders ritually pure in the legal sense discussed in the hadith
key_terms.رَطْبًا: moist; indicating that the impurity ruling remains if wetness persists
key_terms.قَذِرًا: filthy or impure due to najasah such as urine
key_terms.يَبِسَ: dried; the condition required for permissibility in this ruling

ai.seo_question: Does the sun purify impure ground so that salat can be performed on it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the purification of earth by the sun. It states that if an impure spot on the ground is dried by sunlight, salat on it becomes permissible, but not if it remains moist or if it is dried by something other than the sun. It is significant in discussions of taharah and prayer rulings regarding impure ground surfaces.
